name: HeadShift
summary: Head pointing with pointer acceleration: the head cursor runs ahead of the head during fast turns and slows down for fine positioning, so you turn your head less and select more precisely.
howItWorks: Instead of a cursor fixed in the display centre and moved 1:1 with the head, a transfer function sets the cursor gain from head movement: an acceleration-driven fast mode (gain up to 1.5, 3.85 or 6.05 in the Low, Medium and High variants) for ballistic turns, and a speed-driven moderate mode (gain 0.5–1.2) for corrections. The cursor may lead the head vector by at most 15°, keeping it within a comfortable eye-in-head range; upward gain is reduced so offsets settle slightly below centre. No target information or mode switch is needed. In a Fitts' law study (N=28, HTC Vive Pro Eye, controller click to confirm) all variants had lower error rates than plain head pointing at similar movement time, and Medium/High needed less head movement; in three VR applications (N=16, Quest Pro) High cut head movement and effort and was preferred by 10 of 16 users.

relationships.note: Adds dynamic control-display gain to head pointing.
